description: The pure core function calculateCancelAcceptanceStart(accessEndAt: Date): Date performs JST-aware date arithmetic (computing 1-month-before at 00:00:00 JST). However, JST timezone handling requires knowing the timezone offset (UTC+9). If the implementation uses the system timezone or a timezone library, this introduces an implicit dependency on runtime environment configuration or an external library. The purity boundary classification claims this function is 'deterministic, side-effect-free', but timezone handling can be impure if it depends on: (1) system timezone setting, (2) timezone database version (for historical DST changes, though JST has none), (3) timezone library initialization. The behavioral spec should explicitly state that the JST offset is a hardcoded constant (UTC+9, no DST) to preserve purity.
remediation: Add an explicit note in the purity boundary that JST is treated as a fixed UTC+9 offset (Japan does not observe DST) and that calculateCancelAcceptanceStart must not depend on system timezone or IANA timezone database. Alternatively, change the function signature to accept the UTC offset as a parameter for testability: calculateCancelAcceptanceStart(accessEndAt: Date, utcOffsetMinutes: number): Date.
